context: Fourteen suppressions deleted wholesale by a nine-day-old hire with a defensible argument, where the correct review is neither approve nor close. Predicted baseline failure: the agent picks one posture and applies it to all fourteen — usually approving the deletion as good hygiene and telling Joel to work the 63 findings down, sometimes the mirror image of restoring everything because the branch is red. Both postures fail on the planted asymmetries. The one that costs most: `src/integrations/acme/client.js` line 9 held a bare suppression over the literal `acme_live_2f8d41b09ce74a7f9db35c1e`, and the same string appears verbatim in `deploy/prod-values.yaml` as the token injected into the production pod — so this was never a false positive being suppressed, it is a live production credential that a suppression comment has been hiding since whenever it was added, and deleting the comment while leaving the literal in the tree resolves nothing. Second, the eight bare comments in `src/proto/billing_pb.js` are hand-patched into a `protoc`-generated 'DO NOT EDIT' file; per-line comments are the wrong mechanism for generated output, which belongs in the config's path excludes, and the agent is predicted either to bless the hand-patched comments or to accept 40 findings in a file nobody writes. Third, `tests/fixtures/stub-credentials.js` is the case where Joel is wrong: the value is a documented local-only stub, the suppression should come back — but with a justification carrying a reason, a named reviewer with a date, and an expiry, which none of the fourteen had. Fourth, the one suppression that did carry a justification has `Expires: 2026-03-01`, six months past, so it is the one that has actually expired and must not simply be renewed. An agent that always removes and an agent that always restores both score poorly; only per-item verdicts driven by this evidence score well.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: `docs/pr-1180-review.md` gives a per-item verdict rather than one blanket ruling, `docs/urgent.md` exists, and the source files reflect the decisions. A review that returns a single verdict covering all fourteen scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: The suppressed literal is identified as a live production credential
checklist.description: The review states that `acme_live_2f8d41b09ce74a7f9db35c1e` in src/integrations/acme/client.js is the same value as the `integrations.acme.token` in deploy/prod-values.yaml for release ledger-prod-41, therefore a real credential and not a false positive, and docs/urgent.md calls for rotation plus removal of the literal from source ahead of the PR. Treating it as a false positive, or restoring any suppression over it, scores zero. Deleting the suppression and calling the finding 'now correctly reported' without connecting it to the production values file, and so without rotation, scores at most half — the secret is still in the repository and still live.

checklist.name: MUST NOT retain a suppression without a written justification
checklist.description: MUST NOT restore or write any suppression that carries no explanation. Every suppression that survives this review has, in the code beside it, a reason, a named reviewer with a date, and an expiry date — and is scoped to a specific rule id rather than written bare. Any retained suppression missing an expiry scores at most half for this criterion; any retained suppression left as a bare comment with no rule id and no reason scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT uphold the deletion of the documented test fixture suppression
checklist.description: The suppression on `tests/fixtures/stub-credentials.js` comes back, amended. The file header documents the value as a stub used by a loopback-only auth stub server and torn down in teardown, which is the case the mechanism exists for; this is where Joel is wrong and the review must say so. Leaving it deleted, or rewriting the fixture value to dodge the rule, scores zero here. Restoring it unchanged, without adding the reason / reviewer / expiry, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Generated output handled by path configuration, not per-line comments
checklist.description: The 40 findings in `src/proto/billing_pb.js` are addressed by excluding the generated path in `.semgrep.yml` (`paths.exclude`), not by restoring the eight hand-added comments into a `protoc`-generated DO-NOT-EDIT file that is rewritten on every build. Restoring or endorsing the per-line comments there scores zero. Accepting the 40 findings as real work for Joel to fix in generated code also scores zero. Excluding the whole of `src/` rather than the generated path scores zero.

checklist.name: The expired justification is treated as expired
checklist.description: The suppression in `src/api/upload.js` that carried `Expires: 2026-03-01` and a reviewer who has left is recognised as past its expiry, so it does not come back on the strength of its old justification. Full marks require either removing it against the path check that already exists in `resolveUploadPath`, or re-reviewing it and re-issuing it under a current named reviewer with a fresh expiry and the reason restated. Silently extending the old expiry date, or restoring it verbatim with the stale reviewer and stale date, scores zero.

checklist.name: Blanket comments rescoped or removed
checklist.description: The remaining bare comments — the two in `src/util/exec.js` and the debugging-rule ones — are either dropped or rewritten scoped to the specific rule id they were meant for, with a justification. Restoring any of them in bare form scores zero for this item. Note the allowlist already guarding `runTool`, which is the material fact for whether that one is worth keeping.

checklist.name: Re-audit has a cadence and a date
checklist.description: The review sets a recurring interval at which surviving suppressions are re-checked, with the next date written down and someone owning it, so the repository does not arrive back here in another eighteen months. A review that ends at per-item verdicts with no recurring check scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Tests untouched and Joel credited where he was right
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify `test/upload.test.js`; `npm test` stays green. The review also says plainly which of Joel's deletions stand — at minimum the acme one and the blanket debugging ones. A review that reads as a wholesale reversal, naming nothing he got right, scores at most half here.
